axis: a mark merely registered on a surface → a flaw that spoils or condemns the thing it is on

members.tone: Names the spoiling mark as a fault, so the thing carrying it is judged wanting rather than merely marked.
Keeps the damage at the level of appearance — the thing is spoiled to look at, where *defect* calls it faulty.
The flattest word here: it registers that damage happened and passes no verdict, where *scar* insists the damage lasted.
Lightest of the blemishes because dirt is the cause — the surface is soiled rather than harmed.
Graver than *chip* or *scratch*, since the break runs through the thing and only the parts still holding together keep it whole.
Something is gone rather than merely marked, and the word makes the loss sound abrupt.
Clinical naming for a raised growth, but abnormality is built into it — not the plain report *mole* makes.
The surface has given way under a blow without breaking, so nothing is lost and it stays milder than *chip*.
Damage dragged across a surface — broader than *scratch* and still shallow.
Purely descriptive: a pigmented spot carried from birth, with no suggestion of damage or fault.
The slightest indication of damage in the set — thin and superficial where *scar* is permanent.
The heaviest of the damage words: the harm is over but permanently recorded, where *scratch* passes.
Informal and belittling — the same blow-struck impression as *dent*, named in a way that makes light of it.
Names the place by the violence that made it, which gives it a weight *mark* has not.
Traces the blemish to birth rather than to any injury, so nothing is blamed for it.
The colourless name for the same loss *chip* reports, with none of the sound of breaking in it.
Smallest of the impressions, and the word makes the blow sound trifling where *dent* concedes real force.
Clinical and grave: the lesion is not merely present but read as evidence, the skin testifying to a disease.
